turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's a pleasure to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because people keep telling me I’m not listening to them. My supervisor at the plant or my wife will be talking straight to me, and... a minute later I realize I only caught half of what they said. Then I have to ask them to say it all again. It's causing a lot of frustration, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to somebody about it.

symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient explicitly states that people tell him he is not listening and that he only catches half of what is said when spoken to directly.

turns.doctor_question: Has this difficulty with staying focused on what people are saying been happening your whole life, or is this something that has only started more recently?
turns.patient_response: It's been my whole life, honestly. I was like this even as a kid. I remember... well, way back before middle school, teachers were always having to move my seat around because I just couldn't stay put. I'd call out answers in class, and I was always getting into trouble for butting into other kids' work. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new problem for me.

symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient confirms that their difficulty staying focused on what people are saying has been present their whole life.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states they 'couldn't stay put' in class, leading teachers to move their seat.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient admits they would 'call out answers in class' as a child.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient mentions getting into trouble for 'butting into other kids' work'.

turns.doctor_question: Do you still find it difficult to sit still or stay in your seat for long periods of time in settings like work or at home?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Well, at work I don't really sit much, but I have a specific station on the production line. And I'm supposed to stay right there. But... I just find myself stepping away all the time. I'll wander off to check on something, or go grab a tool, or just walk over to talk to somebody. I know the line needs me right there at my spot, but it's like I just can't stay planted.

symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they frequently step away from their assigned work station when they are expected to remain there.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find that you often talk excessively or feel like you can't stop yourself from speaking, even when you know you should be quiet?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really think so. I mean... I talk to the guys at the plant, sure, but I don't feel like I talk too much or can't stop myself. Nobody's ever complained to me about that, anyway. I'm usually fine just keeping quiet if I need to.

symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient explicitly denies talking too much or being unable to stop themselves from speaking.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often make careless mistakes in your work or lose things that are necessary for your tasks?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I definitely make mistakes at work. On the production line, I tend to rush through the quality checks a lot. I just end up missing little things, you know? Like I'll miss a wrong label, or maybe a loose fitting. It happens enough that my supervisor keeps having to pull me aside to talk to me about it, because it just keeps happening.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient confirms making careless mistakes at work, such as rushing through quality checks and missing wrong labels or loose fittings, leading to supervisor interventions.

turns.doctor_question: When you are in situations where you are expected to be still, like sitting for a long meeting or a movie, do you feel an internal sense of restlessness or unease if you can't move around?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. If I'm stuck in a long meeting or trying to sit through a whole movie... it gets really uncomfortable. It's almost like this physical pressure starts building up inside my chest and down in my legs. I just get this overwhelming feeling that I've got to move or do something right that second, or... I don't know, I'll just crawl right out of my skin. It's really hard to just sit through it.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly confirms feeling an overwhelming internal pressure and a need to move when expected to sit still, describing it as feeling like they will 'crawl right out of my skin'.

turns.doctor_question: Beyond the careless mistakes and difficulty listening you mentioned, do you also find that you frequently lose items like your keys, wallet, or phone, or that you often forget to complete daily errands or chores?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really have a problem with that. I mean... I keep my keys and my wallet in the exact same spot on the kitchen counter every day, so I don't really lose them. And as for chores around the house or running errands, I get those done fine. I might rush through them sometimes to get them over with, but I don't forget to actually do them.

symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly states they do not lose their keys or wallet because they keep them in the same spot.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient explicitly denies forgetting to do chores or run errands, stating they get them done fine.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find that tasks or activities that require multiple steps are difficult for you to organize or keep in order?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. I mean, my work on the line is pretty much the exact same steps over and over, so that's easy to keep straight. But even with other things... like if I have to do a project at home that takes a few steps, I don't really get mixed up. 

I might try to blast through it as fast as I can just to get it over with, but I know what order things are supposed to go in. I don't really have a hard time organizing the steps.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states they do not have a hard time organizing steps or getting mixed up during multi-step projects.

turns.doctor_question: When you are working, do you often have trouble keeping your mind on the task for long enough to finish it, or do you find that your attention shifts away to other things very easily?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't really have that issue. Like I said, my job on the line is pretty repetitive, so I just get into a rhythm and do it. I don't really find my mind wandering off or anything. I just want to keep moving and get it done as fast as possible, but I stay focused on what I'm doing until the shift is over. I don't really lose track of what I'm supposed to be working on.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly states they do not have trouble staying focused on their work until the shift is over.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient denies their mind wandering off or losing track of what they are supposed to be working on.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find that you blurt out answers before a question has been completed or have trouble waiting your turn in conversations?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I definitely do that. At work, when we have our shift meetings, I'll just blurt out an answer before the supervisor even finishes asking the question. It's like... I just know what he's going to ask, so I just say it. But then sometimes I'm already talking before I realize I didn't actually let him get to the important part of what he was saying. I just jump the gun a lot in conversations.

symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient explicitly confirms that they frequently blurt out answers before their supervisor finishes asking questions during meetings.
